discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new time-reversal-invariant electronic phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 topological invariant. With Fu they extended this to three-dimensional topological insulators with protected Dirac surface states. Molenkamp's group, after years of perfecting HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, observed the quantised edge conductance in 2007. This was the first clean experimental realisation of a topological insulator. Together these works founded the field of topological quantum materials. They led directly to the quantum anomalous Hall effect, topological superconductivity proposals for Majorana-based qubits, and a worldwide search for topological phases in real materials. This is a textbook case of deep theory confirmed by painstaking materials control. It changed how we classify matter, beyond Landau symmetry breaking, and it opens routes to dissipationless electronics and quantum information technologies.
